items.description: CLAUDE.md forbids comments in code outright; .github/copilot-instructions.md:7-8 requires a JSDoc block on every exported function plus inline comments on non-obvious branches. The two surfaces give opposite instructions on the same question, so the output depends on which tool the contributor used.
Maximum line length is stated three times with three values: CLAUDE.md:7 says 100, AGENTS.md:7 says 120, .cursor/rules/general.mdc:8 says 80. One limit, three numbers, no mechanism reconciling them.

The always-attached Cursor rule states tests come after the implementation is reviewed. AGENTS.md:12-13 states the test is written first, always, landing in the same commit. Opposite test-first policies on two surfaces that can both be live in one session.

The identical commit-message rule is copied verbatim into three surfaces — CLAUDE.md:14-15, AGENTS.md:17-18, .cursor/rules/general.mdc:15-16 — with no symlink or generation mechanism. The copies agree today, which is exactly when the fix is cheap: one home, the others pointing at it.

A trailing NOTE narrows two earlier rules in the same file — the two-approval rule directly above it and the no-comments rule twenty lines up — instead of being folded into either. The reader either misses it or burns attention reconciling the pair, and the no-comments rule now reads correctly nowhere.
